messages:
security-team: @channel Security announcement: were rolling out an automated sweep to reduce credential blast radius. Any service token or API key with an effective TTL > 24 hours will be flagged and then revoked after a 14-day remediation window. Read below for steps. :exclamation:

Omar Ruiz: Does this include keys already stored in Vault with rotation enabled?

security-team: Short answer: no, if Vaultrotation keeps the effective lifetime under 24h you're OK. The sweep targets static keys and tokens recorded in the central token inventory as >24h.

Ivy Park: How do I find my serviceentries quickly?

security-team: Owners with inventory access can run the quick query:
```
SELECT service, token_id, ttl_hours, owner
FROM token_inventory
WHERE ttl_hours > 24;
```
We'll also publish a CSV of flagged services in the policy page.

SRE oncall: Migration tips: prefer OIDC for CI, short-lived STS tokens for infra, and KMS/HSM protect where possible. If you need time, open an "ephemeral-exception" ticket in #eng-sre with justification and compensating controls (IP allowlist, HSM, strict logging). Exceptions are temporary and reviewed.

ops-bot: scheduled: dry-run-sweep at 2026-05-05T16:00Z (no revokes). Enforcement run set for 14 days after dry-run.

security-team: Action items: 1) Run inventory query and check flagged tokens, 2) Migrate to <24h flows or OIDC, 3) Rotate any static keys immediately, 4) File exception tickets if migration impossible. We'll post a short migration checklist and host an office hour tomorrow.

Omar Ruiz: Acknowledged  will start rotating keys this afternoon.

Ivy Park: Opening exception ticket for our nightly batch worker (can't use OIDC until infra upgrade).

security-team: Thanks everyone. Ping us for pairing or follow-up.
